notes: Conference hall: the speaker at the lectern on stage, a seated audience as crowd, the man standing in the aisle among them gives the answer from the hall. Translated line by line; 'жрали' kept coarse as 'stuffing ourselves'.
title: Without Women

lines.text: A rally of feminist organisations is under way.
At the podium, yet another woman speaker is ranting furiously:
What would these men do now without women?!
Well, what would they do without us?!
Huh?! I'm asking you!
What, what?! We'd be stuffing ourselves with coconuts in paradise!

notes: Conference hall: the speaker at the lectern on stage, a seated audience as crowd, the man standing in the aisle answers from the hall. Translated line by line; 'fressen' keeps the coarse 'жрали'.
title: Ohne Frauen

lines.text: Ein Treffen feministischer Organisationen.
Am Rednerpult wettert schon wieder eine Rednerin:
Was würden diese Männer jetzt ohne Frauen machen?!
Na, was würden sie ohne uns machen?!
Hä?! Ich frage Sie!
Was, was?! Wir würden im Paradies Kokosnüsse fressen!

notes: The list stays with the narrator word for word. The man is shown at three ages by the living-room New Year tree: a boy with a letter, a teenager, then the father who walks in as Ded Moroz (red coat, white beard) to his own two kids.
title: Три стадии

lines.text: Три стадии взросления мужчины.
Первая: он верит в Деда Мороза.
Вторая: он не верит в Деда Мороза.
Третья: он — Дед Мороз.

notes: Ded Moroz swapped for Santa Claus as asked; otherwise a literal list. Shown at three ages by the Christmas tree: a boy with a letter, a teenager, then the father who walks in as Santa to his own two kids.
title: Three Stages

lines.text: The three stages of a man growing up.
One: he believes in Santa Claus.
Two: he doesn't believe in Santa Claus.
Three: he is Santa Claus.

notes: Ded Moroz swapped for der Weihnachtsmann as asked; otherwise a literal list. Shown at three ages by the Christmas tree: a boy with a wish letter, a teenager, then the father who walks in as Weihnachtsmann to his own two kids.
title: Drei Stufen

lines.text: Die drei Stufen, wie ein Mann erwachsen wird.
Erstens: Er glaubt an den Weihnachtsmann.
Zweitens: Er glaubt nicht an den Weihnachtsmann.
Drittens: Er ist der Weihnachtsmann.

notes: Narration kept word for word. First the grumpy uncle at the family's dinner table (dining room), then a flyover to the cemetery where the couple, in black, talk on the way back from the funeral.
title: Дядя

lines.text: Жили-были муж с женой, и жили бы они очень счастливо, но поселился у них родственник — дядя.
Оказался этот дядюшка большой сволочью.
Вечно всем был недоволен: то в семье мало зарабатывают, то готовят невкусно, то внимания ему мало уделяют.
Капризами своими всех просто забодал. Но семья была деликатной и всё это терпела.
Наконец этот старый паразит умер.
И, возвращаясь с похорон, муж сказал жене:
Признаюсь тебе, дорогая, что, если бы я не любил тебя так сильно, я бы этого твоего дядю давно выгнал.
Тут жена чуть не падает:
Как? Моего дядю? Я была всегда уверена, что это твой дядя!

notes: Translated line by line. First the grumpy uncle at the family's dinner table (dining room), then a flyover to the cemetery where the couple, in black, talk on the way back from the funeral.
title: The Uncle

lines.text: Once upon a time there lived a husband and wife, and they would have lived very happily, but a relative moved in with them: an uncle.
This dear uncle turned out to be a real swine.
He was always unhappy with everything: the family didn't earn enough, the food wasn't tasty, he didn't get enough attention.
He wore everyone out with his whims. But the family was polite and put up with it all.
At last the old parasite died.
And on the way back from the funeral, the husband said to his wife:
I have to confess, darling, that if I didn't love you so much, I would have kicked that uncle of yours out long ago.
His wife nearly falls over:
What? My uncle? I was always sure he was your uncle!

notes: Translated line by line. First the grumpy uncle at the family's dinner table (dining room), then a flyover to the cemetery where the couple, in black, talk on the way back from the funeral.
title: Der Onkel

lines.text: Es waren einmal ein Mann und eine Frau, und sie hätten sehr glücklich gelebt, aber bei ihnen zog ein Verwandter ein: ein Onkel.
Dieser liebe Onkel entpuppte sich als ein großer Mistkerl.
Ständig war er mit allem unzufrieden: mal verdiente die Familie zu wenig, mal schmeckte das Essen nicht, mal bekam er zu wenig Aufmerksamkeit.
Mit seinen Launen machte er alle fertig. Aber die Familie war taktvoll und ertrug das alles.
Endlich starb der alte Schmarotzer.
Und auf dem Heimweg von der Beerdigung sagte der Mann zu seiner Frau:
Ich muss dir gestehen, Liebling: Wenn ich dich nicht so sehr lieben würde, hätte ich diesen Onkel von dir längst rausgeworfen.
Da fällt die Frau beinahe um:
Was? Meinen Onkel? Ich war immer sicher, dass das dein Onkel ist!

notes: Narration kept word for word ('охрененного' is not mat, kept). The man lies by the bed in a white undershirt from the start; the dog runs in from off screen and comes up to him before the narrator's line about it.
title: Шарик

lines.text: Мужик просыпается с о-хре-ненного похмелья: голова как свинцом налита, руки-ноги как чужие, не подымаются.
Ну, он кое-как повернулся на бок и жалобно так, с надрывом стонет:
Ша-арик... Ша-а-арик...
Подбегает пёс, скулит, лижется.
Мужик на него как дыхнёт и говорит из последних сил:
Ищи!

notes: Sharik becomes Rex (the dog puppet's English name); the command is 'Find it!', what an English speaker tells a tracking dog. The dog runs in from off screen to the man by the bed.
title: Rex

lines.text: A man wakes up with a hell of a hangover: his head feels full of lead, his arms and legs feel like someone else's and won't lift.
Somehow he rolls onto his side and moans, ever so pitifully, with a sob:
Re-ex... Re-e-ex...
The dog runs up, whining, licking him.
The man breathes right on him and says with the last of his strength:
Find it!

notes: Sharik becomes Bello (the dog puppet's German name); 'Such!' is the German tracking-dog command, a direct match for 'Ищи!'. The dog runs in from off screen to the man by the bed.
title: Bello

lines.text: Ein Mann wacht mit einem höllischen Kater auf: Der Kopf wie mit Blei gefüllt, Arme und Beine wie fremd, sie lassen sich nicht heben.
Irgendwie dreht er sich auf die Seite und stöhnt ganz jämmerlich, herzzerreißend:
Be-ello... Be-e-ello...
Der Hund kommt angerannt, winselt, schleckt ihn ab.
Der Mann haucht ihn kräftig an und sagt mit letzter Kraft:
Such!

notes: Narration kept word for word. The officer hands the envelope to the recruit in the office among other candidates; then the bathroom with the toilet, where he opens it and reads the note aloud so a character delivers the punchline.
title: Совершенно секретно

lines.text: В ФСБ набирают работников.
После предварительного собеседования всем вручили конверты с грифом «Совершенно секретно!» и попросили отнести в такой-то кабинет.
Один чувак зашёл по пути в сортир и вскрыл конверт. Там написано:
Вы нам подходите! Возвращайтесь обратно!

notes: FSB becomes 'the secret service' as allowed; the rest is literal. The officer hands the envelope over in the office among other candidates; then the bathroom with the toilet, where the recruit reads the note aloud.
title: Top Secret

lines.text: The secret service is hiring.
After a preliminary interview, everyone was handed an envelope stamped 'Top Secret!' and asked to take it to a certain office.
One guy stopped by the toilet on the way and opened the envelope. It said:
You're just what we need! Come on back!

notes: FSB becomes 'der Geheimdienst' as allowed; the rest is literal. The officer hands the envelope over in the office among other candidates; then the bathroom with the toilet, where the recruit reads the note aloud.
title: Streng geheim

lines.text: Der Geheimdienst stellt Leute ein.
Nach einem ersten Vorstellungsgespräch bekamen alle einen Umschlag mit dem Stempel „Streng geheim!“ und sollten ihn in ein bestimmtes Büro bringen.
Ein Typ ging unterwegs aufs Klo und machte den Umschlag auf. Darin stand:
Sie passen zu uns! Kommen Sie zurück!

notes: Narration kept word for word; 'суки' softened to 'заразы' in text. The man sits on the toilet in the bathroom with a ringing phone in hand that he can't answer.
title: Ещё и в дверь

lines.text: Звонили оба сотовых телефона, верещал стационарный.
Настойчиво вопил Скайп.
Хозяин квартиры, сидящий на унитазе, истерично кричал:
В дверь позвоните кто-нибудь, заразы, ещё и в дверь!
lines.uncensored: В дверь позвоните кто-нибудь, суки, ещё и в дверь!

notes: Skype kept (widely known); 'суки' softened to 'you jerks', original in uncensored. The man sits on the toilet in the bathroom with a ringing phone in hand that he can't answer.
title: The Door Too

lines.text: Both cell phones were ringing, the landline was shrilling.
Skype was wailing insistently.
The owner of the apartment, sitting on the toilet, was screaming hysterically:
Somebody ring the doorbell, you jerks, the doorbell too!
lines.uncensored: Somebody ring the doorbell, you bitches, the doorbell too!

notes: Skype kept (widely known); 'суки' softened to 'ihr Mistkerle', original strength in uncensored. The man sits on the toilet in the bathroom with a ringing phone in hand that he can't answer.
title: Auch noch die Tür

lines.text: Beide Handys klingelten, das Festnetztelefon schrillte.
Skype dudelte hartnäckig.
Der Wohnungsbesitzer saß auf dem Klo und schrie hysterisch:
Klingelt doch noch einer an der Tür, ihr Mistkerle, auch noch an der Tür!
lines.uncensored: Klingelt doch noch einer an der Tür, ihr Arschlöcher, auch noch an der Tür!

notes: Words kept; 'на хера' softened to 'на фига' in text. Breakfast at the kitchen table; the narrator gives the fork throw.
title: Каждое утро

lines.text: Немолодые супруги, уже отметившие серебряную свадьбу, давно живущие вместе, сидят утром за столом, завтракают.
Жена смотрит на мужа долгим взглядом и спрашивает:
Толик, пожалуйста, скажи мне — ты меня всё ещё любишь?
Мужик раздражённо швыряет вилку на стол.
Люся, ну вот объясни мне — ну на фига начинать каждое утро со скандала?
lines.uncensored: Люся, ну вот объясни мне — ну на хера начинать каждое утро со скандала?

notes: Tolik and Lyusya become Joe and Linda (the puppets' English names); 'на хера' softened to 'the heck', original in uncensored. Breakfast at the kitchen table.
title: Every Morning

lines.text: An older couple, who have already celebrated their silver wedding anniversary and have lived together a long time, are sitting at the table one morning, having breakfast.
The wife gives her husband a long look and asks:
Joe, please, tell me: do you still love me?
The man irritably throws his fork down on the table.
Linda, just explain it to me: why the heck start every morning with a fight?
lines.uncensored: Linda, just explain it to me: why the fuck start every morning with a fight?

notes: Tolik and Lyusya become Horst and Gabi (the puppets' German names); 'на хера' softened to 'zum Geier', original strength in uncensored. Breakfast at the kitchen table.
title: Jeden Morgen

lines.text: Ein älteres Ehepaar, das schon die Silberhochzeit gefeiert hat und lange zusammenlebt, sitzt morgens am Tisch und frühstückt.
Die Frau sieht ihren Mann lange an und fragt:
Horst, bitte, sag mir: Liebst du mich noch?
Der Mann wirft gereizt die Gabel auf den Tisch.
Gabi, jetzt erklär mir mal: Wozu zum Geier jeden Morgen mit einem Streit anfangen?
lines.uncensored: Gabi, jetzt erklär mir mal: Wozu zum Teufel jeden Morgen mit einem Streit anfangen?
